summary: Jamaica is visa-free for citizens of the US (for up to six months), Canada, the UK, most of the EU and most Commonwealth countries, though the period is 90 days for some passports and 30 for others, including France, Spain and most of Latin America. CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months, and a few nationalities can buy a visa at the port of entry. Whatever your nationality, every arriving passenger must present Jamaica's free immigration and customs (C5) form, completed online before travel where possible or on paper.

VA.notes: Visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days; every arrival must still present the free Immigration/Customs C5 form, best completed online before traveling.

VE.notes: Visa-free for up to 30 days as a visitor, per PICA's visa-requirements table; complete the online C5 form before departure.

VN.notes: A visitor's visa must be obtained from a Jamaican mission or honorary consulate before traveling. There is no visa on arrival and no eVisa.

YE.notes: A visitor's visa must be obtained from a Jamaican mission or honorary consulate before traveling. There is no visa on arrival and no eVisa.

ZM.notes: Commonwealth citizens are admitted visa-free for up to 90 days; the free C5 immigration and customs form, online or on paper, is still mandatory.

ZW.notes: A visitor's visa must be obtained from a Jamaican mission or honorary consulate before traveling. There is no visa on arrival and no eVisa.

conditionalWaivers.text: Tourists from Albania, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Kazakhstan, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Romania, Serbia and Honduras who hold a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa may enter Jamaica without a Jamaican visa for 30 days or less. All except Honduras must also carry proof of vaccination against measles, rubella and polio.

fee.notes: PICA's processing fee for an extension of stay, from its Immigration Processing Fee schedule. Staying beyond the visa-exemption period costs JM$50,000. A visitor's total stay is capped at 12 months for Commonwealth citizens and 6 months for others.

passportValidity.text: Jamaica requires a passport valid for the whole of your intended stay rather than a fixed six months. Airlines and many home governments still advise six months' validity, so travel with six months where you can.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (yellow card)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you are arriving from, or have recently transited, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — mainly parts of tropical Africa and South America, and also Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean. Travelers coming directly from Europe or North America do not need one to enter Jamaica.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states whether travel insurance is required to enter Jamaica. The UK Foreign Office advises checking before you travel that you have appropriate travel insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK FCDO travel advice — Jamaica health

onwardTicket.text: All visitors must hold a return or round-trip ticket to a country they are allowed to enter.

source.name: Embassy of Jamaica, Washington DC (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade) — Requirements for entry into Jamaica

proofOfFunds.text: All visitors must be able to show evidence of sufficient funds to support themselves during their stay. No amount is published.

source.name: Embassy of Jamaica, Washington DC (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade) — Requirements for entry into Jamaica

declarations.name: Immigration/Customs (C5) form
declarations.submitWindow: Online before arrival where possible; a paper form is also accepted
declarations.text: All arriving passengers must present a completed and signed Immigration/Customs C5 form, either filled in online before travel or on paper. It is free, so any site charging a fee for a Jamaican "travel authorization" is not official — if you are unsure, check with your airline or PICA.

currencyLimits.text: Cash and negotiable instruments worth USD 10,000 or more (or the Jamaican dollar equivalent) must be declared to Jamaica Customs on arrival and departure.

notes: Firearms and ammunition are prohibited without a permit obtained in advance — visitors have been arrested and jailed over a single forgotten round in hand luggage.
Cannabis is decriminalised in small amounts for personal use inside Jamaica, but carrying any across the border in either direction remains a criminal offense and airport screening catches it.
Camouflage-patterned clothing is restricted and can be confiscated from civilians.
Fresh produce, plants and meat products are controlled; declare anything agricultural on the C5 form.

payments.text: Resorts, hotels, supermarkets and chain restaurants take cards and often quote prices in US dollars. Route taxis, jerk stands, craft markets and rural shops are cash-only in Jamaican dollars, and the exchange rate you get paying US cash in a shop is rarely a good one.

safety.text: Crime and homicide rates in Jamaica are high, but gang violence and shootings mostly occur in inner-city areas, including parts of Kingston, Spanish Town and Montego Bay, and tourist areas are not usually affected. Most attacks on tourists are robberies. Hotels and resorts are generally well guarded, and some visitors have been followed and robbed on the way from the airport to private accommodation.

source.name: UK FCDO — Jamaica: safety and security

bestTimeToVisit.text: Mid-November to mid-April is dry and least humid, and covers the main winter season and Reggae Month in February. Late summer is hot, wet and the peak of hurricane season.

idp.text: Jamaica is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Jamaica yet.

tips.text: Complete the free Immigration/Customs C5 form at enterjamaica.gov.jm before you fly and save the QR code. Sites charging a fee for a "Jamaica travel authorization" are not official — that authorization was discontinued after the pandemic and no longer exists.

Bringing a firearm or even one round of ammunition into Jamaica is a serious offense and has led to visitors — including licensed gun owners who simply forgot — being arrested and held for months. Empty and check every bag before you travel.
Small amounts of cannabis are decriminalised for personal use within Jamaica, but taking it across the border in either direction is still a criminal offense. Do not attempt to fly home with any.

Driving is on the left, roads are narrow and overtaking is aggressive. Use licensed red-plate taxis or hotel transfers rather than unmarked cars, and agree the fare before setting off — meters are rare.

Jamaica's departure tax and airport fees are normally bundled into your airfare. Check your ticket breakdown rather than assuming, and keep some cash for the airport if your carrier is a small regional one.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Jamaica?
faq.answer: Probably not. Jamaica is visa-free for citizens of the US, Canada, the UK, most EU and Schengen countries, Japan, South Korea, much of Latin America and most Commonwealth countries, and CARICOM nationals get six months. The period depends on the passport: PICA's table gives six months to US citizens, 90 days to, among others, Germany, the Netherlands, the Nordic countries, Brazil, Mexico and South Korea, and 30 days to France, Spain, Portugal, Japan and most of Latin America. Some nationalities, such as Armenia, Georgia and Uzbekistan, can get a visa at the port of entry for US$100; others need a visitor's visa from a Jamaican high commission or embassy before traveling. There is no eVisa.

faq.question: What is the Jamaica C5 form and is it mandatory?
faq.answer: The C5 is Jamaica's combined immigration and customs declaration. It is mandatory for every arriving passenger regardless of nationality, and it is free. PICA accepts it either online at enterjamaica.gov.jm or as a signed paper form; the UK government advises completing it online before you arrive where possible.

faq.question: Do I still need a Jamaica Travel Authorization?
faq.answer: No. The Jamaica Travel Authorization introduced during the pandemic has been discontinued; the online C5 immigration/customs form replaced it. Third-party sites still selling a "travel authorization" are charging for something that does not exist — if in doubt, confirm with your airline or PICA before paying anyone.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Jamaica without a visa?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport: PICA's visa-requirements table allows 30 days for some nationalities, 90 for others and six months for US citizens. The officer writes the actual period on your stamp and may grant less if your return ticket is sooner. Extensions are handled by PICA and must be applied for before your stamp expires; a visitor may stay at most 12 months in total as a Commonwealth citizen, or 6 months otherwise.

faq.question: How much passport validity do I need for Jamaica?
faq.answer: Officially, your passport must be valid for the whole of your stay rather than a fixed six months beyond it. In practice airlines apply the stricter six-month rule at check-in, so travel with six months' validity where possible.

faq.question: Is Jamaica safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Resort areas and the main tourist corridors are heavily policed and most visits are trouble-free, but Jamaica's homicide rate is high and several inner-city districts carry standing "do not travel" warnings from the US and UK. Stick to licensed taxis, avoid displaying valuables, and do not walk unfamiliar areas after dark.
